blocks.prompt: 4 (i) Given the function \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\). Find the equation of the function after: vertical stretch by factor 2
blocks.explanation:
One vertical scaling of \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\).
A vertical stretch by 2 is \(y = af(x)\) with \(a = 2\): multiply the whole function by 2.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\), \(x \ge 0\).
To find: the function after a vertical stretch by factor 2.
Method: vertical scaling \(y = af(x)\); \(a > 1\) stretches vertically by \(a\).

Apply the stretch
\[y = 2f(x)\]
\[y = 2\sqrt{x}\]
Why: every output of f is doubled; the input x is unchanged.

Check:
The point \((4, 2)\) of \(\sqrt{x}\) becomes \((4, 4)\); and \(2\sqrt{4} = 4\). The domain stays \(x \ge 0\).

blocks.prompt: 4 (ii) Given the function \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\). Find the equation of the function after: horizontal shift 3 units to the right
blocks.explanation:
One horizontal shift of \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\).
A shift 3 units right is \(y = f(x - h)\) with \(h = 3\): replace \(x\) by \(x - 3\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\).
To find: the function after a shift of 3 units to the right.
Method: horizontal shift \(y = f(x - h)\); right means \(h > 0\), so \(h = 3\).

Replace \(x\) by \(x - 3\)
\[y = f(x - 3)\]
\[y = \sqrt{x - 3}\]
Why: the graph moves right when x − h is put in place of x.

Check:
The starting point \((0, 0)\) moves to \((3, 0)\): \(\sqrt{3 - 3} = 0\). The domain becomes \(x \ge 3\).

blocks.prompt: 4 (iii) Given the function \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\). Find the equation of the function after: applying both transformations (i) and (ii).
blocks.explanation:
Both transformations, in the order (i) then (ii).
First stretch: \(g(x) = 2\sqrt{x}\). Then shift \(g\) 3 units right: replace every \(x\) in \(g\) by \(x - 3\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \sqrt{x}\).
To find: the function after the vertical stretch by 2 and then the shift 3 units right.
Method: apply (i), name the result, then apply (ii) to it.

Step 1: vertical stretch by 2
\[g(x) = 2\sqrt{x}\]
Why: this is the answer of part (i).

Step 2: shift g 3 units right
\[y = g(x - 3)\]
\[y = 2\sqrt{x - 3}\]
Why: the shift acts on the current function \(g\); only its \(x\) changes, the factor 2 stays.

Check:
The point \((1, 1)\) of \(\sqrt{x}\) goes to \((1, 2)\) after the stretch and to \((4, 2)\) after the shift; \(2\sqrt{4 - 3} = 2\). Doing the shift first gives the same result here, because one change is vertical and the other horizontal.
